finding: Training memory is much higher than inference memory for distilgpt2.
evidence: Training used around 4.7x to 4.8x more peak allocated memory than inference under comparable settings.
importance: Training memory needs separate modeling from inference memory.

finding: Training memory increases with sequence length, but fixed training components dominate.
evidence: Peak allocated memory increased from 1592.43 MB at 32 tokens to 1616.71 MB at 128 tokens.
importance: Sequence length matters, but parameters, gradients, and optimizer states dominate in this setup.

evidence: Peak allocated memory increased from 1600.19 MB at batch size 1 to 1648.43 MB at batch size 4.
importance: Model weights, gradients, and optimizer states are shared across the batch.

finding: AdamW optimizer state is a major contributor to training memory.
evidence: AdamW used 1600.94 MB peak allocated memory while SGD used 956.49 MB.
importance: Optimizer choice must be included in training memory prediction.

finding: AdamW optimizer state can be approximated as 2x parameter memory.
evidence: Estimated optimizer-state memory was 624.94 MB; observed AdamW-SGD peak difference was 644.45 MB.

finding: Backward temporary memory correction significantly improves training prediction.
evidence: Allocated MRE improved from 15.66% in V1 to 2.98% in V2.
importance: Backward temporary memory is a required component for training prediction.

finding: A 5% safety margin removes dangerous fit/fail failures.
evidence: Dangerous failures reduced from 7 to 0, while accuracy improved from 91.07% to 91.96%.
importance: Makes the estimator safer for scheduling-style decisions.
